content.title: About
content.content: The “Multigrain” muffin is a soft baked good made from whole grains such as oats, barley, and rye. It has a light nutty note, moderate sweetness, and a dense yet tender crumb. Ideal for breakfast or a snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The recipe blends five different whole grains, boosting fiber content.
No artificial flavors or colorings are used in the muffins.
Each muffin provides about 30 % of the adult daily iron requirement.
The dough relies on natural gluten from whole grains, not on gluten substitutes.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Whole grains increase dietary fiber, supporting healthy digestion.

items.title: Source of complex carbs
items.content: Complex carbohydrates deliver sustained energy and prolonged satiety.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamins B1, B2 and B6 aid metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Mineral content
items.content: The muffin supplies magnesium, iron and zinc, important for muscle and immune health.

items.title: Low added sugar
items.content: Sweetness comes from natural fruit purées, without refined sugar.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Contains wheat, barley and rye, making it unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: Despite nutritious ingredients, the muffin is relatively calorie‑dense; consume in moderation.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: A modest amount of salt is added; those monitoring sodium intake should take this into account.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the muffin as a standalone snack, split and spread with low‑fat cottage cheese, add to yogurt, or use as a base for an avocado toast.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep muffins in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3 days or refrigerate for up to 7 days. For longer storage, freeze in a freezer‑safe bag for up to 3 months.
